boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Messiah rituals and recurring campus practices, from candlelit bookends to finals-week pancakes and a midnight scream.

cards.title: Begin with Candlelight
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week, Messiah University
cards.notes: Attend the first-year move-in-day worship gathering with families; it formally welcomes the new class into the Messiah community.
cards.short_summary: A candlelit Welcome Week ritual for new students and their families.
cards.evidence_claim: Messiah identifies a candlelight worship service at the end of first-year move-in day as one of two ceremonies that bookend a student's time there.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of Welcome Week for first-year students and families; confirm the annual program before attending.

cards.title: End with Candlelight
cards.subtitle: Baccalaureate, Messiah University
cards.notes: Look for the final candlelight worship gathering held the night before Commencement, a deliberate counterpart to first-year move-in.
cards.short_summary: The graduating-side bookend to Messiah's candlelight tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Messiah says its second candlelight worship service occurs at Baccalaureate the night before Commencement.
cards.access_notes: Part of Baccalaureate programming before Commencement; check the University's commencement schedule for details.

cards.title: Follow the Bagpiper to Soccer
cards.subtitle: Homecoming, Covered Bridge to soccer field
cards.notes: Wear the provided white shirt and join the bagpiper-led walk across the Covered Bridge before the Homecoming soccer games.
cards.short_summary: A white-clad, bagpipe-led Homecoming procession to the soccer field.
cards.evidence_claim: Messiah documents a Homecoming White-out March in which students in free white T-shirts follow a bagpiper across the Covered Bridge to the soccer field.
cards.access_notes: Occurs before the Homecoming soccer games; the University states that students receive white T-shirts.

cards.title: Homecoming Powderpuff
cards.subtitle: Homecoming, Messiah University
cards.notes: Watch or join the Homecoming matchup format: women play football while men cheer, with class years paired as opponents.
cards.short_summary: A class-versus-class Homecoming football and cheerleading switch-up.
cards.evidence_claim: Messiah describes Powderpuff Football as a Homecoming tradition with women playing football, men serving as cheerleaders, and class-year matchups.
cards.access_notes: A Homecoming activity; participation and spectator arrangements vary by year.

cards.title: Take the Day to Serve
cards.subtitle: Spring semester, Messiah University
cards.notes: Sign up for the spring service program, when classes and work pause so students and employees can serve on campus or locally.
cards.short_summary: A spring day when the campus shifts from classes to service.
cards.evidence_claim: Messiah says Service Day gives students and employees a spring day off from classes and work to serve together through Special Olympics or local outreach opportunities.
cards.access_notes: Held each spring; available service options and sign-up details are announced by Messiah.

cards.title: Pancakes and Tots at Lottie
cards.subtitle: Lottie Dining Hall, finals week
cards.notes: During finals week, stop by Lottie for the late-night pancake-and-tot service staffed by employee volunteers.
cards.short_summary: A late finals-week snack service of free pancakes and tots.
cards.evidence_claim: Messiah states that Lottie Dining Hall opens one finals-week night from 10 p.m. to midnight for employee volunteers to serve free pancakes and tots.
cards.access_notes: The official page specifies one finals-week night from 10 p.m. to midnight; confirm the selected night each term.

cards.title: The Finals-Week Midnight Scream
cards.subtitle: Residence halls, finals week
cards.notes: At midnight during finals week, listen for the collective campus release; participate only in ways that respect quiet-hours and neighbors.
cards.short_summary: A collective midnight stress-release during finals week.
cards.evidence_claim: Messiah says students hold a collective scream from their windows at midnight every night during finals week.
cards.access_notes: Occurs at midnight during finals week; follow current residence-life guidance and be considerate of others.

cards.title: Make the Creek Part of Campus
cards.subtitle: Yellow Breeches Creek, Messiah University
cards.notes: Use the campus-running creek for a daytime hammock break, study session, tubing, canoeing, or fishing within applicable safety rules.
cards.short_summary: The creek that Messiah lists among its campus traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Messiah includes Yellow Breeches in its campus-traditions section and says students use the creek for hammocking, studying, tubing, canoeing, and fishing.
cards.access_notes: Use only lawful, safe access and appropriate water-safety practices; conditions and permissions can change.

cards.title: Powerhouse Worship
cards.subtitle: Weekly campus worship event
cards.notes: Check the campus worship calendar for Powerhouse, the longstanding weekly music-centered worship event for Messiah students.
cards.short_summary: A weekly worship gathering described as part of the Messiah experience for decades.
cards.evidence_claim: Messiah describes Powerhouse as a weekly event that has, for decades, been part of the student experience through worship music.
cards.access_notes: Weekly scheduling is subject to the current Campus Ministries calendar.

cards.title: Let Students Lead Thursday Chapel
cards.subtitle: Thursday mornings, Messiah University
cards.notes: Attend a Thursday morning chapel to experience the student-led format, offered alongside educator-led small groups around campus.
cards.short_summary: A recurring chapel format led by students on Thursday mornings.
cards.evidence_claim: Messiah states that Thursday morning chapels are student-led, with educator-led small groups taking place around campus at the same time.
cards.access_notes: Regular chapel programming is for the Messiah community; consult Campus Ministries for the current schedule and attendance expectations.
